verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's reliability docs describe configurable fallbacks. After num_retries a failed call falls back to another model group, configured via `fallbacks=[...]`, with the proxy looping through the specified groups. The Router adds cooldowns, timeouts, retries, and specialized content_policy_fallbacks across deployments and providers. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration that fallback works reliably in production.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can configure automatic fallback to another model or provider when one fails

citations.quote: If a call fails after num_retries, LiteLLM falls back to another model group, so a failing model or provider automatically fails over to a healthy backup.
litellm proxy will loop through all the model_groups specified in `fallbacks=["gpt-3.5-turbo"]`
Basic reliability logic - cooldowns, fallbacks, timeouts and retries (fixed + exponential backoff) across multiple deployments/providers.
content_policy_fallbacks: For litellm.ContentPolicyViolationError - LiteLLM maps content policy violation errors across providers
